Torrential Rains Trigger Landslides, Disrupting Cable & Satellite Sites in Northern Vietnam

A series of intense rains across northern Vietnam this week has triggered multiple landslides, significantly impacting the Cable & Satellite industry's operational sites in the region. Several uplink stations and satellite ground facilities have reported structural damage and service disruption, with local management teams scrambling to ensure safety and continuity.

The most heavily affected area is Lao Cai province, where persistent downpours since Sunday night have led to soil slippage and flooding at the primary satellite gateway operated by VietSatLink. A spokesperson for VietSatLink stated, "Our site suffered partial power loss and minor building collapse. While core transmission infrastructure remains intact, staff have been evacuated as a precaution." The facility, located on a hilly outcrop, is a critical node for regional uplink and downlink services.

Other firms, including Thanh Phat Broadcasting and SkyRoute Services, have reported similar challenges at their satellite receiving stations and cable headends in Yen Bai and Ha Giang provinces. In one case, muddy debris inundated a control room, forcing a temporary shutdown while workers began clearing operations. "We are monitoring slope stability and weather updates closely to protect our teams and equipment," said Nguyen Van Hai, site manager at SkyRoute Services.

According to the Vietnam Cable & Satellite Industry Association, at least five facilities have reported moderate to severe disruption as of Wednesday afternoon. "The landslides are a stark reminder of the region's vulnerability during the monsoon period," commented association chairwoman Le Thi Thu. "Member firms are prioritizing safety protocols and emergency response, but ongoing rainfall means the situation remains fluid."

Early estimates suggest that at least 120 industry workers have been displaced from affected sites, with some being temporarily relocated to alternate company housing. Emergency crews are working to stabilize slopes and reinforce facility perimeters, though access remains hampered in several remote areas.

The full extent of the damage is still being assessed as rainfall continues across the northern highlands. Industry representatives have called for increased coordination on disaster response measures and long-term investments in site resilience given the changing climate patterns.
